summary: useApiError correctly contains the trust boundary at the localization layer. The composable never reads any string field from the raw error (no message/stack/toString); it only extracts a numeric status, normalizes it via Number()+Number.isFinite, and uses it strictly as a numeric key fragment. The te()-gate before every t() neutralizes the production silent-fallthrough risk that would otherwise leak internal key paths (e.g. 'errors.profile.saveName.401') to end users — Decision 9 sets silentTranslationWarn: true, so an unguarded t() on a missing key would return the key verbatim, and this implementation explicitly prevents that. The terminal fallback returns '' when even 'errors.generic' is absent rather than echoing the lookup key — this is the correct fail-safe. contextKey is interpolated only into the i18n lookup path (no eval, no DOM sink, Vue templates auto-escape the returned string). Only one minor robustness concern: property reads on the unknown error and the Number(raw) coercion are not wrapped in try/catch, so a malicious upstream error with a throwing getter on statusCode/status/response.status, or a value with a throwing valueOf/Symbol.toPrimitive, would cause the handler to throw rather than return a safe localized string. This propagates an exception to the caller — it does NOT embed sensitive content into the returned message — so it is an availability/robustness concern, not an information-disclosure one. Verdict: OK; the design satisfies the security intent of Decision 10.

non_blocking_findings.category: A04: Insecure Design (defensive coding at trust boundary)
non_blocking_findings.title: extractStatus does not isolate throws from hostile error shapes
non_blocking_findings.description: The handler consumes `error: unknown` from useApi, which crosses a trust boundary. extractStatus performs unguarded property reads (`e.statusCode`, `e.status`, `e.response?.status`) and a `Number(raw)` coercion. If an upstream error object exposes a throwing getter on any of these properties, or `raw` is an object whose `valueOf`/`Symbol.toPrimitive` throws, the handler will throw rather than resolve to a safe localized string. No raw error content reaches the user via the returned message (the catch path does not embed `error.message`/stack), so this is not a direct information-disclosure issue — but it does break the contract that the composable always returns a safe string, which is the security guarantee Decision 10 is meant to provide. In practice useApi is the only known producer and the shapes are well-formed, so exploitability is low.
non_blocking_findings.impact: A malformed/hostile error from a future producer could cause the handler to throw inside a Vue catch-block, surfacing an unhandled exception in production rather than the intended safe localized message. Not exploitable for data exfiltration; impacts robustness/UX of the safety net.
